description: Several mailbox writes the user approves at once, e.g. outlook_create_folder then outlook_create_rule filing into it with refs {"moveToFolder": "0.id"}, or a handful of moves and flags. There is no rollback: if an op fails, the ones before it stay applied and the rest do not run. A write Outlook did not confirm (a timeout or server error after sending) is not a failure here: its result carries status "unknown" and the batch goes on, so check each result before relying on it. To move MANY messages matching a condition (a sender, an age, read state), use outlook_move_messages instead — one call, one confirmation for the whole set. Run up to 100 writes with ONE preview and ONE approval, in order, stopping at the first failure (no rollback: the result says which ops were applied). Each op is {tool, args, refs?}; args are exactly what that tool takes (without confirmToken). refs feeds an earlier op's output into an argument, e.g. {"tool": "…", "args": {…}, "refs": {"expense_id": "0.expense_id"}} takes expense_id from op 0. Writes available: outlook_mark_read, outlook_update_message, outlook_move_message (produces newId), outlook_create_rule, outlook_update_rule, outlook_delete_rule, outlook_create_folder (produces id), outlook_update_folder. Asks the user to confirm first: a confirmation prompt where the client supports one; otherwise the first call returns a preview and a confirmToken, and only a repeat call with that token proceeds (see MCP_CONFIRM_MODE).

confirmToken.description: ONLY for the two-step confirmation fallback (a client without MCP elicitation). The confirmToken from this same tool's phase-1 "confirmation-required" response, passed back ONLY after the user has seen that preview and explicitly approved it in chat — never on the first call, never invented, never reused. Call again with the same arguments. Ignored when the client supports elicitation.
